steps.what: Develop industry standards of product safety through evidence assessment and technical deliberation

tasks.design: Retain standards development and technical deliberation with the engineer using {DOCS}. A reusable document structure supports work without establishing a separate drafting burden or deciding acceptable product risk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standards need defensible evidence and agreement across differing product contexts.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing technical records and collaborative documents support standards work.
tasks.still_hard: Choose requirements that are effective, testable and proportionate.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve technical trade-offs and defend proposed requirements.
tasks.altitude: Own the evidence and reasoning behind product safety requirements.

evidence.claim: Standards development retains substantive technical judgement; a measured repetitive drafting subtask is not established.

assumptions: The baseline is technical standards development, not invented document formatting.
Committee adoption and publication remain separate from this proposed contribution.
No new automation service or maintenance is introduced.
research_questions: Is repetitive evidence assembly measurable separately from deciding requirements?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Standards reasoning and deliberation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain emergency-response liaisons with outside organisations

steps.what: Maintain liaisons with fire departments, mutual aid societies and rescue teams for emergency responses

tasks.design: Keep emergency-response liaison and cooperation with the engineer using {EMAIL} and {DOCS}. A contact list supports the relationship without proving readiness or replacing discussion of changing capabilities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reliable cooperation depends on shared understanding and actual partner capability.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication channels support relationship maintenance.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve assumptions about roles, access and available assistance.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust and agree practical cooperation with response partners.

evidence.claim: Emergency-response liaison retains relationship and coordination time; a contact database alone establishes no saving.

assumptions: The baseline is liaison rather than a separate meeting-booking or contact-entry process.
External partners' participation remains existing external work; no labour transfer or automation saving is claimed.
No new automation or added maintenance is proposed.
research_questions: Is repeated contact maintenance a measurable burden distinct from substantive liaison?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Relationship and response coordination remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and conduct industrial hygiene research

steps.what: Plan industrial hygiene research questions, exposure measurements and study methods
Conduct industrial hygiene research and assess exposure evidence and limitations

tasks.design: Retain study design, workplace investigation and interpretation using {DOCS}, {SPREADSHEET} and {OTHER}, industrial hygiene measurement equipment. Existing instrument calculations do not establish a new saving in research judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exposure research depends on representative measurements and defensible methods.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing measurement equipment and analytical tools support investigation.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish representative exposure from misleading samples or confounding factors.
tasks.human_edge: Connect workplace reality to valid exposure evidence.
tasks.altitude: Own the validity of industrial hygiene research.

reach.task: Evaluate sampling validity and exposure interpretation

evidence.claim: Industrial hygiene research retains design, fieldwork and interpretation time; no repeated automated pipeline is established by the task.

assumptions: OTHER denotes industrial hygiene measurement equipment.
Measurement collection, data checks and interpretation remain in s2 rather than assuming free structured exposure data.
Routine incident statistics belong to the separate statistical task and receive no duplicate saving.
No new automation service or upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which repeated calculation or data preparation components are not already handled by instruments?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Study planning, fieldwork and scientific interpretation remain.

tasks.short: Compile and interpret occupational illness and accident statistics

steps.what: Compile occupational illness and accident records and validate definitions, dates and exposure denominators
Calculate statistical counts and rates from the checked occupational illness and accident dataset
outputs: traceable counts, rates and trend tables

steps.what: Analyze and interpret statistical patterns, reporting bias and uncertainties before drawing safety conclusions
inputs: traceable counts, rates and trend tables

tasks.design: Configure native summaries in {OPS_SYSTEM} or controlled {SPREADSHEET} calculations, using {BI} only for a useful shared view. Keep classification checks, denominator validation and interpretation with the engineer; rising reports are not automatically worsening safety.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated statistical consolidation can obscure time for interpretation and data-quality checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records and deterministic formulas can produce traceable counts and rates.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish real changes from reporting differences and incomplete health information.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret uncertainty without converting a trend into an unsupported causal claim.

ambition.what: Review checked statistical patterns between periodic reports.

tasks.altitude: Move repeated calculations into controlled reporting while retaining interpretation.

reach.task: Resolve authorised illness categories and reporting completeness
reach.learn: Health data quality and denominator control

evidence.claim: Deterministic counts and rates are feasible with validated incident classifications and exposure denominators; the proposed savings are model knowledge.

assumptions: Incident officers and authorised health-data custodians produce event IDs, event dates, reporting periods, permitted illness or accident categories and correction versions; payroll or operations supplies exposure hours with population and period definitions.
In s1 the engineer captures, reconciles and validates those fields plus exclusion and duplicate rules; all focal capture and classification checks remain in its 40 hours.
Four added other-role hours cover source corrections and authorised health-data preparation rather than treating structured classifications as free inputs.
Missing categories or invalid denominators remain explicit and return to manual reconciliation in s1 and interpretation in s3; the report never invents an illness category or causal finding.
Use existing record summaries and controlled formulas before custom analytics; eight added focal hours cover definition changes, reconciliation and formula validation.
The view uses only authorised aggregated data; individual case assessment and clinical data handling remain with their responsible professionals.
research_questions: Does deterministic reporting save calculation time after classification, denominator checks and source correction effort?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75; gross 25 minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net 17. E1 range 0-12 allows existing summaries and incomplete denominators; interpretation remains fully counted.

role.ambitious_version: A safety engineer who reviews traceable occupational statistics with less repeated calculation while retaining the relationships and judgement needed for effective safety work.
